newsitem.title: UK: UK MEDIA WATCHDOG CHASTISES JINGOISTIC TABLOIDS.
newsitem.headline: UK MEDIA WATCHDOG CHASTISES JINGOISTIC TABLOIDS.

text.p: Britain's media watchdog on Wednesday castigated British tabloid newspapers for their coverage of the Euro 96 soccer championships, saying it was offensive and in bad taste.
The Press Complaints Commission said anti-German headlines run before England's semifinal clash with Germany had "significantly misjudged the public mood".
The Sun said "Let's Blitz Fritz," the Daily Mirror's banner headline proclaimed "Achtung Surrender" and The Daily Star said: "Herr We Go. Bring On The Krauts."
The coverage prompted 300 complaints to the commission from British readers. The German government and the German team did not complain.
Germany won the semifinal on penalties before beating the Czech republic in the final.
The Daily Mirror pointed out to the commission it had apologised to readers for any offence caused and The Sun and Daily Star said the jokes it made were "good-natured."
